substantive_reconstruction.canonical_coefficients: The operative Lean definition coefficientSeries is exp(X)*invOneSubPow(k+1), and coefficientPolynomial truncates at k+1, i.e. retains degrees0..k. coefficientSeries_coeff expands it as sum_(m=0..r) choose(k+r-m,k)/m!, exactly the candidate's coefficients. m<=r ensures the natural subtraction has its ordinary nonnegative meaning; every factorial is nonzero, including0!=1. At r0 the unique term is choose(k,k)/0!=1. Evaluation at0 therefore gives A_k(0)=1 for every natural k. For k=0, canonical A_0=1; the deliberately noncanonical constant2 meets degree<=0 but doubles both requested endpoint values, showing only the old standalone normalization gap.
substantive_reconstruction.coordinate_and_jets: SourceInterpolant is taylor1 of q*F_k(X)+F_k(1-X), with q=exp(-1), so sourceInterpolant_eval is precisely H_k(p+1). Physical nodes -1,0 become0,1 and dt/dp=1 adds no scale to derivatives. F_k(t)=(1-t)^(k+1)A_k(t) has a zero of multiplicity at least k+1 at1: each Leibniz term in a derivative j<=k retains a positive power of1-t and vanishes there. F_k(1-t)=t^(k+1)A_k(1-t) has the analogous opposite-node zeros at0. Reflection may supply(-1)^j in derivatives, but zero remains zero; it does not manufacture the own-node values. The source separately derives those from the formal truncation identity, which the candidate correctly does not claim follows from the factors alone.
substantive_reconstruction.values_and_weights: F_k(0)=1,F_k(1)=0, so H_k(0)=q,H_k(1)=1 and S_k(-1)=q,S_k(0)=1. The q weight stays on unreflected F_k, as the actual source definition requires. For k=0, F_0=1-t,H_0=q(1-t)+t; all endpoint/zero-jet claims still hold. The case j=0 is included, rather than only positive derivative orders.
substantive_reconstruction.exact_weighted_reflection: For any real a,b define H_(a,b)(t)=a F_k(t)+b F_k(1-t). The polynomial identity H_(a,b)(1-t)=H_(b,a)(t) holds for ALL a,b,t, including zero coefficients, with no division. Reflection swaps the ordered shapes and correspondingly reverses the coefficient pair. For the actual pair(q,1), H_k(1-t)=qF_k(1-t)+F_k(t), not qH_k(t), H_k(t), or any fixed scalar multiple globally.
substantive_reconstruction.zero_and_nonzero_denominators: For the actual weights, H_k(0)=q>0,H_k(1)=1, so evaluating a proposed global H_k(1-t)=cH_k(t) legitimately gives c=1/q at t=0 and c=q at t=1, a contradiction since0<q<1. No zero denominator is concealed in that endpoint test. More generally the necessary/sufficient coefficient equations are b=ca,a=cb: a=b=0 gives the zero polynomial and every c works; exactly one nonzero coefficient makes such c impossible; both nonzero allow only b=a,c=1 or b=-a,c=-1. This handles cases that would be lost by dividing by a or b without checking them.
substantive_reconstruction.pointwise_ratio_limit: If one instead writes a pointwise ratio H_k(1-t)/H_k(t), it is defined only where H_k(t)!=0. On[0,1], the canonical nonnegative coefficients and constant1 give A_k>=1, and the two nonnegative endpoint shapes are not simultaneously0, so H_k>0 there. Outside that interval no global nonzero-denominator claim follows: for k0 the root t=-q/(1-q) gives H_0(t)=0 while H_0(1-t)=1+q>0. The candidate avoids this trap by using the division-free reflected polynomial identity and nonzero endpoint evaluations.
